fatal_errors: The proposed nanohierarchical treatment does not reconstruct the target intervention: varying Mo content in SPS-fabricated CoCrFeNiMox-Ni/MoS2-Ag-Cr2O3 composites.

The intervention is not operationally defined; it alternates between an unspecified thermomechanical treatment and an unspecified alloy-design adjustment without identifying precipitate chemistry or processing parameters.
The baseline is homogeneous CoCrFeNi rather than the Mo0.2 self-lubricating composite containing Ni-coated MoS2, Ag, and Cr2O3.
The cited evidence concerns Ni50(AlNbTiV)50 and does not establish that the same nanohierarchical architecture can be created or will remain stable in CoCrFeNi.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses wide-temperature sliding in air and proposes a controlled treated-versus-untreated comparison, so it is a scientifically plausible alternative at a broad conceptual level. The cited paper directly supports adaptive low-temperature stress accommodation and an 800 °C nanocrystalline glaze in another complex concentrated alloy. However, it misses the target composition, Mo-series intervention, SPS processing, Si3N4 counterface, 8 N load, speed, distance, and temperature-resolved behavior. Its mechanism omits Mo-induced FCC distortion, sigma-phase strengthening, low-temperature MoS2/Ag lubrication, and high-temperature NiO/silver-molybdate tribofilms. Claims of low friction are also less well supported than the cited evidence's wear-rate claims. The falsification experiment is directionally useful but cannot be reproduced until the treatment, precipitate chemistry, load, speed, distance, and statistical design are specified.
